key_insight: Coherent turbulence structures are not automatically causally important: only about half of identified Q events drive the surrounding flow more than an equivalent volume of incoherent turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Flow-control strategies should target not just visible structures, but the local flow environment and interaction patterns that determine whether a structure is truly causally significant.
method: Compared causal significance of identified Q events against matched volumes of incoherent turbulence.
Used feature-based analysis to identify which local flow quantities distinguish high-causality structures.
Applied conditional averaging to link those features to upstream and wall-attached flow interactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that only about half of the identified structures were causally more significant than an equivalent volume of incoherent turbulence, revealing strong variability across event types.
watch_item: Quadrant-based coherent structures are dynamically heterogeneous, so causal interpretations can be misleading if local strain and vorticity context are ignored.
paper_title: Coherence does not always imply causality in wall-bounded turbulence
